transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, mostly it’s that I just can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore. I’m a carpenter, so there’s always noise, you know—one saw starts up, or somebody walks past the office, or I suddenly think about another job I was supposed to look at, and I’m gone. Like completely pulled off what I was doing.

And then I’ll realize half the day went by and I didn’t finish the thing right in front of me. It’s been getting really frustrating.
Have you struggled with staying focused like this since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only started recently?

No, it’s not new. I mean, I can remember it all the way back in grade school, before I was even 12. Teachers used to tell my mother I was bright, but careless—which, you know, I hated hearing that. Like I wasn’t trying.

I’d lose homework, or forget the instructions right after they gave them, and I’d be sitting there staring out the window while everybody else was finishing their seatwork. I remember one classroom had these big windows facing the playground, and if there was a bird or somebody mowing grass outside, forget it… I was gone. So yeah, it’s been around a long time.

Besides the trouble focusing, do you notice yourself feeling physically restless or fidgety, or acting impulsively—like interrupting people, blurting things out, or having trouble sitting still for long periods?

Yeah… I do get that wound-up feeling, especially if I’m stuck at the desk doing estimates or sitting through a long meeting. It’s like my body is saying, get up, go check something, move around—even though I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish.

It’s funny, because after my wrist healed I thought, okay, now I can just sit and catch up on paperwork, but sitting there almost makes me feel more restless. Like I’m not in pain or anything, I just feel all keyed up inside.

When you feel that restless, keyed-up feeling, is it usually tied to specific worries or anxious thoughts running through your mind, or is it more just a physical urge to move regardless of what you're thinking about?

It’s more like a body thing, I think. I mean, I’m not sitting there thinking, “Oh no, what if this or that happens.” It’s more… if I’m at the desk doing estimates, or stuck in some long meeting, I just get wound up inside and feel like I need to get up and move around.

Which is annoying, because I know I’m supposed to stay put and finish the thing. And my wrist is healed now, so it’s not like that’s the reason. I’ll start thinking, well, maybe I should go check on the truck, or see if something needs doing in the shop—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. It’s just that sitting still makes me feel all keyed up.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, finishing other people's sentences, or blurting things out before someone finishes speaking?

Um… I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’m the kind of person who’s always jumping in and cutting people off, at least not that I’ve noticed.

I mean, sometimes in a conversation I’ll think I know where somebody’s going, and then my mind is already on the next thing—but whether I actually say it out loud before they’re done, I don’t know. My daughter would probably have a better answer for that than me. I tend to notice more when other people interrupt me, which is funny, because maybe I do it too and don’t catch it.

Sorry, I’m kind of going around it. I guess I’d say I haven’t really noticed blurting things out much.
Do people who know you well—like your daughter or coworkers—ever comment that you talk more than others, or that it's hard for you to stay quiet during conversations or meetings?

I don’t really know. I can’t think of anyone saying, like, “you talk too much” or anything like that.

My daughter might say I repeat myself sometimes, but that’s different, I guess. And at work, meetings are usually more about getting through the job list, so I’m not sitting there chatting a bunch—though sometimes I’ll have something I want to say and then I lose track of it if I wait too long. But, no, I don’t think people comment that I can’t stay quiet. Not that I’ve noticed, anyway.

Do you often find yourself getting up and leaving your seat in situations where you're expected to remain seated, like during meetings or dinners, or having trouble waiting your turn in line or in conversation?

Yeah, I mean… in meetings especially, or if I’m stuck at the desk doing estimates, I get this wound-up feeling inside, like I need to stand up or go do something. I know I’m supposed to just stay there and finish, but it’s hard.

It’s not because of my wrist anymore—that’s healed—though for a while I think I blamed that. Now it’s more just sitting there too long makes me feel like I have to move around. I don’t know so much about waiting in line, but the sitting still part, yeah, that happens.
Outside of work meetings, do you have trouble relaxing or engaging in quiet activities—like watching TV, reading, or sitting through a movie—without feeling the urge to get up or stay busy?

Yeah… yes, I do. At home even, if we’re supposed to be just sitting and watching something, I’ll start tapping my foot or shifting around, and then I’m up getting a glass of water or checking something for no real reason.

Church is probably where I notice it the most, because it’s quiet and you’re supposed to just sit there. I’ll catch myself whispering something to my husband, or fidgeting, or moving around in the pew, and I know I’m probably being distracting. It’s not that I’m trying to be rude, it’s just… sitting still in that quiet can feel almost unbearable sometimes.

And then I start thinking, “Did I leave the laundry in?” or “I should move that pile of tools,” even if it has nothing to do with anything. Sorry, that’s probably not what you asked. But yes, quiet sitting is hard for me.
